title: DSA Interview Recall: 62 Problems, Nine Pattern Shelves
description: A finite active-recall journey through every problem in Umar Farooque’s captured DSA roadmap, organized by interview trigger, invariant, complexity, and edge cases.
audience: An interview candidate returning to DSA after a long break who previously solved these roadmap problems
prerequisites: Prior exposure to the 62 problems in the source roadmap
Comfort with Python-like pseudocode and Big-O notation
Willingness to attempt each challenge before revealing the answer
learningOutcomes: Recognize the dominant pattern for every captured roadmap problem
State the invariant and complexity before starting implementation
Recover binary-search, pointer, hashing, string, linked-list, and stack techniques
Identify dangerous edge cases and contract details under interview pressure
Build a 1-day, 7-day, and 21-day review queue from actual recall misses

blocks.title: Matrix Search
blocks.learningObjective: Recall the interview trigger, invariant, and implementation plan for Matrix Search.
coreFacts: Binary search over a virtually flattened matrix
If B exists, it remains inside the current flat index interval.
O(log(N·M)) time and O(1) space

standard.hook: Interview trigger: Binary search over a virtually flattened matrix.
body: Search target B in an N×M matrix whose rows are sorted and whose next row starts at or after the previous row’s last value.
Approach: Search indices 0…N·M−1 and read matrix[mid // M][mid % M]. Compare with B and discard one half.
bullets: Invariant: If B exists, it remains inside the current flat index interval.
Complexity: O(log(N·M)) time and O(1) space
Watch: Empty input, one cell, and values repeated across a row boundary.

blocks.title: Matrix Median
blocks.learningObjective: Recall the interview trigger, invariant, and implementation plan for Matrix Median.
coreFacts: Binary search over the value domain plus per-row upper bounds
count(≤x) is monotone, so the median is the first value reaching the target rank.

Every value at or below the true floor root is feasible; every larger value is not.

blocks.title: Special Integer

coreFacts: Binary search on window length with a sliding-window predicate

Complexity: O(N log N) time and O(1) extra space
